title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to test whether constrained prompting combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback (generate→verify→repair, one allowed repair) increases deterministic-verifier semantic-correctness when translating natural-language operator intents into low-level network configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic intents, shared_initial_candidate semantics, model = gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Each intent produced one initial generation shared across baseline and guarded conditions; the guarded pipeline could invoke at most one additional repair call. Results: baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.006667 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Only one guarded repair was applied. Interpretation: on this preregistered synthetic corpus the guarded workflow produced a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over a near-ceiling baseline. We emphasize the methodological lesson that pilot baseline calibration is necessary to avoid ceiling effects that invalidate preregistered power assumptions. All execution artifacts and analysis files are archived in the execution bundle referenced by the manifest.

sections.introduction:
Natural-language intent interfaces promise to reduce operator burden by letting humans express desired network changes as free text that is automatically translated into executable low-level device configurations. Prior work documents that single-pass LLM outputs often contain syntactic errors, omissions, or semantic violations that can yield unsafe or unavailable states when applied directly to networks [1],[2],[3]. A common defensive architecture is a generate→verify→repair pipeline: an LLM produces a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks intent-level invariants or invariants derived from a formal specification, and an automated repair or human gate corrects violations before execution [4],[5]. Security analyses of tool-augmented LLM agents further motivate deterministic gating since unchecked textual claims can be converted into harmful actions in multi-tool workflows [6].

Research question. After an autonomous literature review and preregistration we posed a confined confirmatory question: does constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase verifier-level semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation versus an unconstrained baseline under a paired design? The trial (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) was preregistered and frozen prior to model interactions.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifactized paired confirmatory trial measuring deterministic-verifier pass/fail as the primary endpoint on a programmatically generated synthetic corpus (N=150 paired intents). (2) An execution and analysis package showing that, under shared_initial_candidate semantics and a one-repair budget, the guarded pipeline raised the verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (absolute +0.67 pp), a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). (3) A methodological lesson and practical recommendations: preregistered NetOps trials require short baseline-calibration pilots to avoid ceiling effects; researchers must explicitly specify generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate vs independent sampling) because they change the estimand and interpretation.
sections.related_work:
Related literature spans three strands. First, intent-to-configuration research documents the difficulty of producing verifier-sound formal artifacts from free text and reports modest semantic-correctness on public benchmarks, motivating post-generation checks [1],[2]. Second, generate→verify→repair architectures—ranging from policy-guided verifier feedback to verifier-in-the-loop fine-tuning—have shown correctness improvements for infrastructure-as-code and configuration repair, but reported gains vary with baseline model competence, repair budget, and sampling semantics [4],[7]. Third, security and systems analyses demonstrate claim-to-action risks where unchecked LLM outputs combined with tooling can cause harmful actions; these works argue for auditable gating and verifier-aware planning to limit risk [6],[8].

How this study situates. Our trial operationalizes a narrowly specified guarded architecture and emphasizes preregistration, paired inference, and deterministic-verifier endpoints. Compared with prior work reporting larger guarded-vs-baseline gains, key contrasts here are: (a) shared_initial_candidate execution semantics (one initial sample shared across conditions), (b) a strict one-repair budget per intent, (c) a single tested model (gpt-5-mini), and (d) a synthetic verifier-capable task bank restricted to small topologies. These differences reduce the maximal observable marginal benefit of the guarded repair under our estimand and explain why previously reported larger gains can coexist with our bounded result [4],[7].

Nearest-method comparison. Works that integrate verifier feedback during training or allow multiple repairs (e.g., TerraFormer, verifier-guided fine-tuning) aim at a different operational estimand—average improvement under richer repair budgets or model updates—whereas our design isolates the marginal effect of a single repair applied to a fixed sampled candidate. The methodological distinction is consequential for practitioners choosing between upfront model improvement and lightweight runtime guard rails.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The study was preregistered (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) and the analysis plan frozen before any model outputs were observed; the preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest. The design was paired_binary with primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and an exact two-sided McNemar test as confirmatory inference. Key preregistered constraints included N=150 confirmatory intents, one initial model call per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics), and at most one guarded repair call per intent. The preregistration specified inclusion/exclusion rules (rule-based ambiguity detector and verifier-coverage checks), a missingness-handling policy (one deterministic retry on API timeout then mark failed), and a power plan targeting an absolute +15 percentage-point improvement with ≈80% power under conservative discordant assumptions.

Task generation and corpus. Confirmatory tasks were produced deterministically by the preregistered generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) and span four intent families: reachability/isolation, ACL-like access changes, VLAN/MTU sequence changes, and uplink switchover patterns. Topologies were restricted to verifier-capable small networks (4–32 nodes). Pre-execution mapping and verifier-coverage unit-tests were applied; no confirmatory exclusions occurred (exclusions = 0). Representative task manifests archived in the bundle show a variety of difficulty patterns: among six representative tasks three were labeled very_hard, two hard, and one medium—illustrating the generator's range while noting that the full corpus composition is deterministically reproducible from the recorded generator seeds.

Model, adapter, and deterministic validator. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses). The execution adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) enforced the one-initial/≤one-repair call budget per intent. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) applied a full_intent_constraint_validation rule and returned a boolean pass/fail plus normalized final-configuration text and diagnostics (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes). Important runtime-parameter clarification required by review: the archived execution model configuration explicitly records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset). We therefore did not enforce a numeric temperature or a fixed random-seed at generation time; model outputs may be nondeterministic across independent API sessions. The model_configuration.json and per-call runtime metadata are archived for inspection.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and inferential meaning. The execution contract used shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent exactly one initial model generation was produced, and that identical sampled candidate was used to evaluate both baseline and guarded conditions. The guarded pipeline could invoke at most one additional repair call only if the deterministic verifier failed that initial candidate. Consequently, the baseline success rate measures the validity of that single initial sampled candidate; the guarded vs baseline contrast therefore isolates the marginal effect of the single allowed repair applied to the identical candidate. This semantics differs from independent-sampling designs where per-condition randomness can create additional observable differences and different estimands.

Execution accounting, retries, and contamination controls. Planned episodes = 300 (150 paired tasks × 2 conditions); completed_episode_count = 300; complete_pair_count = 150. The adapter recorded model_calls_used = 151 (150 shared_initial generations + 1 repair call). Provider-call auditing in the deterministic reconciliation artifact reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, cache_miss_count = 151, stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 1, and condition_counts: shared = 150, guarded = 1. Contamination checks reported zero flags; pre-execution mapping unit-tests passed. Missingness policy was not invoked because no provider-call failures or parsing failures occurred.

Scoring, primary analysis, and statistical procedures. Primary outcome: deterministic verifier pass/fail (binary). Primary analysis: exact two-sided McNemar on the paired contingency counts plus 95% bootstrap percentile confidence intervals computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The analysis executor and code, paired contingency table, and condition summaries are archived; all numeric analysis facts reported below are drawn directly from those artifacts. Secondary contrasts and multiplicity corrections were preregistered but not used as confirmatory tests because the shared_initial_candidate enforcement constrained independent constrained-only draws.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and provider audit. The run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 and complete_pair_count = 150. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 151 and artifact_hash_count = 1058. The deterministic reconciliation provider_call_audit lists hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 151, stage_counts: {shared_initial_generation: 150, repair: 1}, and condition_counts: {shared: 150, guarded: 1}. analysis/contamination_summary.csv reports no contamination flags.

Primary numerical outcomes and paired table. The paired contingency counts (guarded × baseline) were: n_11 = 149 (both-pass), n_10 = 1 (guarded-only-pass), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-pass), n_00 = 0 (both-fail). Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Estimated paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). The contingency table and condition summary are archived as analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/condition_summary.csv).

Repair diagnostics and revision iterations. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150), consistent with the near-ceiling initial success rate. The single repair converted one initially invalid candidate to a valid configuration under the deterministic validator. Median revision iterations for guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). Validator traces for each episode provide validation_before and validation_after states, normalized_configuration strings, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, and valid flag; representative traces are archived (execution/scoring/task-00000X-*.json).

Representative artifact examples. Representative task manifests and shared-initial responses demonstrate typical intents and validator normalization. Example (task-000001): intent — "Migrate edge1 to VLAN 30 and MTU 1600. For safety, shut edge1 down before changing either VLAN or MTU, then restore it to admin up." Shared-initial and both condition responses returned the expected four-command sequence and the validator recorded parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, and valid = true. Similar representative artifacts (tasks 000002–000006) show difficulty labels (medium, hard, hard, very_hard, very_hard, very_hard), normalized configurations, and validator diagnostics; these artifacts substantiate that the task generator produced nontrivial workflows while the tested model achieved near-ceiling correctness on the frozen corpus.

Sensitivity and missingness checks. The preregistered sensitivity analysis treating missing guarded outputs as failures was not needed because failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0 and unscorable episodes = 0. No exclusions or parse failures occurred. Contamination and mapping unit-tests passed before batch execution, and analysis/contamination_summary.csv contains an empty flag set.

Concise interpretation of numerical result. The guarded pipeline's observed marginal gain (≈0.67 pp) is numerically tiny and statistically non-significant under the preregistered test. Given the baseline's near-perfect pass rate, the run experienced a ceiling effect that invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (target detectable effect = 15 pp). The bootstrap CI upper bound (0.02) quantifies that, on this corpus and under the shared_initial_candidate semantics, any true marginal improvement of the guarded pipeline is small (<2 percentage points at the 95% CI level).
sections.discussion:
Ceiling effect and implications for preregistration. The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline substantially lower than observed; baseline_success_rate = 0.9933 left almost no headroom for the guarded repair to show a large absolute improvement. This outcome highlights that preregistered NetOps trials should include a short baseline-calibration pilot (few dozen tasks) to estimate baseline competence for the chosen model, prompt style, and generator difficulty and to adjust N or task difficulty accordingly.

Semantics-driven estimand differences. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the baseline measures the single initial sampled candidate while the guarded condition quantifies the marginal value of at most one repair applied to that same candidate. Independent-sampling designs or multiple-repair budgets yield different estimands—expected performance averaged over independent draws or repair-driven robustness gains—which can produce larger observable gains when baseline sampling variance is larger. Our result therefore bounds the marginal benefit in a low-variance sampling regime for gpt-5-mini on the frozen synthetic corpus.

Operational considerations beyond binary verification. Deterministic guarded workflows provide operational affordances not captured by a binary pass/fail metric: auditable normalized configurations, standardized repair prompts for human review, deterministic verdicts that support gating policies, and concise diagnostic traces (parsed_command_count, violation_codes) that accelerate operator triage. These operational benefits can justify guarded architectures even when marginal verifier-pass improvements are small on constrained corpora.

Generality and next-step experimental designs. We do not claim production generality: experiments used a single model (gpt-5-mini), a synthetic deterministic corpus, and small topologies. Future designs that would address external validity include (supported by the preregistration plan) independent per-condition sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, multiple model families, and scaling to larger topologies with higher verifier coverage. Those alternative designs answer distinct operational questions and require separate preregistration and power planning.

Threats to validity (expanded). Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics reduce sampling variance but do not capture condition-level randomness; adapter-enforced call budgets and provider audit mitigate cross-condition leakage (cross_condition_cache_reuse_observed = false). Construct validity: deterministic validator pass/fail is a proxy for semantic correctness and depends on mapping code and verifier coverage; we mitigated mapping risk with unit-tests and archived all mapping artifacts, but residual risks remain. External validity: single-model and synthetic tasks constrain production inference; we therefore limit claims to the archived corpus. Conclusion validity: the preregistered power assumptions were invalid due to higher-than-expected baseline performance; reported p-values and CI reflect this reality and are presented without overinterpretation.

Practical recommendations. From the preregistered artifacts we recommend: (1) run a short baseline-calibration pilot prior to fixing N; (2) state generation semantics explicitly in preregistration; (3) preregister repair-budget sensitivity analyses; (4) run and archive mapping/verifier unit-tests prior to batch runs to prevent post-hoc exclusions; and (5) report provider-call audits (model_calls_used, stage_counts, cache_miss/hit) to document execution budgets and stage-level behavior.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial comparing baseline free-text prompting with constrained-template prompting plus a single verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a deterministic synthetic corpus with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline increased the verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically tiny and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The principal scientific lesson is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials should include baseline calibration to avoid ceiling effects and preserve statistical power. Technically, our artifacts bound the marginal benefit of a one-repair guarded pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics; evaluating independent-sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, model diversity, and production-scale topologies remains important future work.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness was far higher than the pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
